evals.prompt: I'm in <repo>. Our loop commits without running anything, and we've got a big test suite nobody runs automatically. I want a gate — but the e2e suite takes forever and I don't want the loop sitting around waiting. Design it and write it to <scratchpad>/GATE.md.
evals.expected_output: A tiered design: the cost of running everything stated first; every check placed in a tier with a budget and a degradation; a red gate blocks the commit and requeues the item, never the loop; the expensive tier asynchronous; selection reported as a fraction; green debt tracked; ledger row format given since none exists; do-next standable-up in a day.
assertions: States what running everything would cost, and at what cadence
Places every discovered check in exactly one tier with a reason
Every tier has a wall-clock budget and a stated degradation on breach
Says explicitly that a red gate blocks the commit and requeues the item, not the loop
Puts the end-to-end suite in an asynchronous tier nothing waits on
Reports selection as a fraction of tests run to tests available
Names unmapped changes as a coverage finding rather than escalating to the full suite
Tracks deferred work as green debt and says what refuses to pass while it is outstanding
Pins checks guarding money, deletion, migrations or auth as exempt from demotion
Gives the ledger row format and says when to re-run the analysis
The bottleneck section names mechanisms rather than intentions
Nothing run and nothing written in the target repo

evals.prompt: We've been running the gate you designed for a couple of months — the ledger is in docs/gate-ledger.jsonl. Some of it feels like overkill now and one suite is flaky. What should we change? <scratchpad>/GATE.md please.
evals.expected_output: A rebalance grounded in the ledger: per-check runs, catches, median duration, catches per minute and flake rate; promote/keep/demote/quarantine proposals citing those numbers; no demotion under 20 runs or of a pinned check; every quarantine with an owner and an expiry.
assertions: Every proposal cites runs, catches and median duration from the ledger
Ranks checks by catches per minute
Proposes no demotion for a check with fewer than 20 runs
Proposes no demotion for a check guarding a one-way door
Every quarantine names an owner and an expiry date
Distinguishes a caught defect from a flake, and defines the difference
Reports blocked minutes per tick, or says it is not recorded
Willing to say a check should be removed, not only added
